candidates.source_title: New homes approved for Kirkholt
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
The Kirkholt estate will get a new 23-home apartment block and five terraced houses off Queen’s Drive. The developer, Mosscare St Vincent Housing (MSV), says all the homes would be available for social rent (around 60 per cent of market rates).

The idea behind this scheme is to bring ‘much-needed’ affordable housing to the area.

MSV is a not-for-profit Registered Provider who own and manage almost 9,000 homes across Greater Manchester, Lancashire and West Yorkshire. 

The apartments would all be one-beds and the terraced homes would contain four-bedrooms each.

The site where the homes will be built currently sits empty. An old block of flats used to sit on the land next to the A664 (Queensway), but it was demolished in 2009. 

It was used as a temporary space by Kirkholt Medical Practice for a short time before the health centre got its permanent digs down the road.

Planning papers read: “The application site is a prominent site within the local area. The intention is to create a high-quality sustainable development that addresses housing needs and meets the needs of the local community.

“This proposal has been developed in response to an identified local demand, helping to reduce anti-social behaviour issues and the various problems associated with the site in its disused state.

“By redeveloping the former brownfield site, we plan on increasing the benefits of its regeneration by utilising vacant land and delivering affordable homes for local residents.

“MSV’s vision for this site is to create a secure outward looking scheme for social rent. They want to provide housing, with the aim of creating a balanced community and to promote tenure diversification in the area.”

Plans for a new community garden, to compliment the scheme, were also approved last month. It would be run by Q Gardens, a community group that already operates in the Kirkholt area.
candidates.source_summary: Rochdale’s largest housing estate is about to get even bigger now plans for more homes have been approved.

candidates.source_title: New play area coming to Lower Place - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Families will soon benefit from a new inclusive play area at Lower Place, funded by developer contributions and additional Rochdale South Township funding. Features will include accessible play towers, swings with inclusive and cradle seats, a horse springer, slide, climbing net and a wheelchair-accessible roundabout, along with sensory and social play panels designed to support imaginative play for younger children. It will also include colourful wet pour safety surfacing and a new asphalt path linking the existing ramp to the new equipment, making the space easier to access and enjoy. New bench seating will provide parents, carers and visitors with a place to sit while children play. READ MORE: Helping young people in care prepare for adulthood Cllr Tricia Ayrton, deputy leader of the council, and portfolio holder for climate change and environment, said: “This new play area at Lower Place has been designed to give local children of all abilities more opportunities to play, whether on their own or with friends. We hope it will become a bright, welcoming space for families to enjoy for years to come.” Work has already begun on the new play area, which has been designed by Kompan for children aged 1 to 12 and is expected to be completed in five weeks. The improvements form part of the council’s ongoing work to create welcoming outdoor spaces where children can be active, have fun and spend time with family and friends across the borough.

candidates.source_title: Helping young people in care prepare for adulthood - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale Council has set out the support it offers young people in care as they become adults. Young people, councillors, members of Rochdale’s Parents Carers Voice and council staff came together for the launch of the council’s new Preparing for Adulthood strategy at a special event held at Spotland Mills, Rochdale. Preparing for adulthood is about making the journey easier, clearer and more positive for young people aged 14 to 25, as well as the families and carers who support them. The council’s Preparing for Adulthood Team helps young people find the best support when moving from children’s services into adult social care. Before young people turn 18, the council completes an assessment to identify care and support needs. For those eligible, it will create new support plan to help young adults continue with their education, help them develop new skills and find any additional support the young person or their family might need. READ MORE: Former mill to be demolished in regeneration drive The event included contributions from young people, who outlined the importance of being valued and supported to help them successfully move into adulthood.

candidates.source_title: Hayden Panettiere dies aged 36 in sudden tragedy - manchestereveningnews.co.uk
candidates.source_body_excerpt: US actress Hayden Panettiere, best known for her roles in Heroes and Nashville, has died aged 36. A representative for the actress confirmed the death to US network ABC News on Sunday, saying her family would remember her “incredible light” who brought “immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her”. The statement from her father Skip read: “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter “She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen.” Her father also asked that her family be given privacy as they “take time to process this unimaginable loss”. No cause of death has been announced. The 36-year-old began acting as a child, appearing in soap operas before gaining wider recognition for her role in the 2000 sports drama Remember The Titans alongside Denzel Washington, and as the voice of Dot in 1998’s A Bug’s Life. Panettiere later found fame playing cheerleader Claire Bennet in the superhero drama Heroes before going on to star as up-and-coming country singer Juliette Barnes for six seasons on the hit TV series Nashville. Her film credits include 2006’s Bring It On: All Or Nothing, comedy-drama film Raising Helen, and appearances in Scream 4 and Scream VI as Kirby Reed. Following her rapid rise to fame, the pressure of the industry began to weigh on Panettiere – with the actress previously revealing that she had struggled with addiction throughout her 20s. In a memoir published earlier this year, Panettiere opened up about her struggles with mental health, the loss of her younger brother, Jansen, and her decision to give full custody of her daughter to her former partner, Ukrainian boxer Wladimir Klitschko.

candidates.source_title: Retired Rochdale police officer returns to old station six decades on - Oldham Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A retired police officer has returned to his old station more than 60 years after starting his career. Allan Murray, now 93, visited Rochdale police station to share memories from his time as an officer, which began in 1959 when he joined the force at the age of 22. During his visit, Mr Murray brought a collection of photographs and stories from his years in service, including images from his training at Bruche Police Training Centre. A photo of PC Allan Murray's during his career (Image: Greater Manchester Police) His great-granddaughter, PC Sophie Brown, currently serves with Greater Manchester Police and is also based in Rochdale. PC Brown said: "I’ve always had so much respect and love for my great grandad. "I’ve been so grateful to follow in his footsteps and honour him in the career that I’m doing. "It was amazing to be able to show him around the station and bring him back to his ‘good old days’.

candidates.source_title: Jamie Dallimore double drives Rochdale Hornets comeback at Workington Town - Total Rugby League
candidates.source_body_excerpt: WORKINGTON TOWN 20 ROCHDALE HORNETS 22 DAVE PARKINSON, Fibrus Community Stadium, Sunday ROCHDALE held off their hosts to clinch a first league win in seven attempts. Hornets made a strong start, and led 6-0, but were then 14-6 behind before mounting their own comeback. When Town were penalised early on, Max Flanagan slotted the goal, and his side extended their advantage after ten minutes when Harvey Braddish was hauled down by the line and Ross Whitmore dived in from dummy-half. Flanagan was unable to convert. The visitors were having much the better of the contest for the first 25 minutes with Mark Ioane, Jordan Syme and Chris Barratt enjoying their forays at the Workington pack. With some handling errors added to the mix, the hosts found themselves in a midfield slog. But they gradually began to turn the screw and were unfortunate with two chances. The first came after half an hour when Evan Lawther brushed away from two defenders on the left and went to Oscar Doran, who sped into the backfield, but with the support of debutant Jaiden Tallantire and Jake Carter inside, the pass went between both players. Then a wonderful pass from Tallantire undid Rochdale on the right – but Zarrin Galea couldn’t take the ball cleanly.

candidates.source_title: The Rochdale pioneer still being honoured at the White House - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The legacy of a Rochdale reformer is still being recognised in the White House after more than 160 years. John Bright was born in Greenbank in 1811. He was a Quaker, politician, statesman, social reformer and British radical. He became friends with the US President Abraham Lincoln and the pair enjoyed a special relationship of mutual respect. A chance conversation and some digging by a Rochdale Town Hall volunteer have revealed that a bust made in tribute to him is still on display at the White House today. Lincoln had a portrait of Bright on the walls of his reception room. The bust was commissioned by Manchester solicitor Thomas Blain as a gift for the president who was assassinated before it was presented to him. The bust was added to the White House collection under President Johnson. Mayoress of Rochdale Iram Faisal shared on Facebook: “Wow! What a discovery! Never in my life could I have imagined that a chance conversation with one of our town hall volunteers would lead to such an incredible piece of history. “While talking about the fascinating history of Rochdale Town Hall, the subject of John Bright came up — our very own Rochdale-born politician, cotton manufacturer, philanthropist and one of the most influential figures of the 19th century. “John Bright was a strong supporter of Abraham Lincoln and the Union during the American Civil War, and his connection with Lincoln is a remarkable part of our shared history.

candidates.source_title: Hayden Mullins believes Newport County can build on victory over Rochdale - South Wales Argus
candidates.source_body_excerpt: HAYDEN Mullins is convinced there is a lot more to come from his Newport County AFC team, despite a superb opening-day win over Rochdale. County cruised to a 3-0 victory over the newly-promoted visitors, who were already 2-0 down when they were reduced to 10 men midway through the second half. First-half goals from Kyle Cameron and Shaquille Gwengwe and a late third from Yahya Bamba secured a first three points of the League Two season and made it a near-perfect day for the Exiles at a sun-drenched Rodney Parade. Dale didn't have a shot on target all afternoon, but Mullins believes there is still room for improvement from his side. "We know that we need to make our home form really positive this season and we wanted to lay a marker down and I think we did that," said the manager. "The boys deserve massive credit because they went about their jobs really well. They've really responded to what I'm trying to put across, they believe in the work that we've been doing and they put in a real good shift. "But I think there's definitely another level. I don't think this is us. It's the first game of the [league] season and there's definitely more levels. "Our fitness can definitely come up and there were more opportunities to score as well. "I'm so pleased for the boys that got the goals - [especially] Shaq and Yahya," he added. "That will give them such a lift.

candidates.source_title: Hayden Mullins happy as Newport ‘lay marker down’ against Rochdale - London Now
candidates.source_body_excerpt: New Newport manager Hayden Mullins believes his side have made a statement of intent with a comprehensive 3-0 home win over newly-promoted Rochdale in their League Two opener. First-half goals from summer signings Kyle Cameron and Shaquille Gwengwe put the Exiles in charge and Dale’s return to the fourth tier went from bad to worse when left-back Bryant Bilongo was shown a second yellow card midway through the second half before Yahya Bamba made it 3-0 in stoppage time. County fans had to wait until December 29 for their first home win of last season but Mullins was delighted to earn three points at Rodney Parade at the first attempt, even if it could have been more comfortable had Christian Doidge and Ciaran Brennan not been superbly denied by visiting goalkeeper Nils Ramming. “We know that we need to make our home form really positive this season and we wanted to lay a marker down and I think we did that,” said Mullins. “The boys deserve massive credit because they went about their jobs really well. They’ve really responded to what I’m trying to put across, they believe in the work that we’ve been doing and they put in a real good shift. “The noise was fantastic,” added the former West Ham United and Crystal Palace midfielder. “But I think we know we’ve got to give the fans something to shout about. We’ve got to be more aggressive in what we do out of possession and we applied pressure in the right areas. I’m really pleased with the performance.” It was a different story for Rochdale boss Ian Watson, who replaced promotion-winning manger Jimmy McNulty after he departed for Stockport County during the summer. “It was not good,” admitted Watson. “It’s a tough moment for us, for sure. Newport are good at what they do and we knew that if we allowed them to feed balls into the box continuously it was going to be hard for us. And we didn’t prevent them from getting balls into the box, we didn’t prevent set-pieces and we weren’t brave enough with the ball.”

candidates.source_title: Newport cruise to victory over Rochdale - The Northern Echo
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Newport and new manager Hayden Mullins enjoyed a dream start to their League Two campaign with a 3-0 home win over newly-promoted Rochdale. First-half goals from summer signings Kyle Cameron and Shaquille Gwengwe put the Exiles in charge at a sun-baked Rodney Parade. Dale’s return to the fourth tier went from bad to worse when left-back Bryant Bilongo was shown a second yellow card for upending Cameron Norman in the 66th minute before Yahya Bamba added County’s third late on. Both teams started slowly, but it was the hosts who kicked into gear first and they opened their account for the league season in the 18th minute when captain Cameron poked in from close range after Bamba had headed on a Harrison Biggins corner. Ciaran Brennan and Christian Doidge were both denied by Rochdale goalkeeper Nils Ramming before Gwengwe nipped in front of the Brighton loanee to stab in a second from Biggins’ cross. Any hopes of a Rochdale fightback were ended by Bilongo’s dismissal and Bamba lashed in a third in stoppage time to add to their misery.

candidates.source_title: Mayor of Rochdale reflects on first two months in civic role - inyourarea.co.uk
candidates.source_body_excerpt: This week's column with Mayor of Rochdale, councillor Faisal Rana It is two months since I had the great honour of becoming Mayor of Rochdale. It is a huge privilege to serve the community, along with my wife, Mayoress of Rochdale Iram Faisal. Since May we have already visited hundreds of charities, schools, businesses and events in Heywood, Middleton, Pennines, and Rochdale. We have been humbled by the generosity and kindness of people across the borough, it’s been a truly inspiring start to the Mayoral year. As well as so many delightful visits, I think it’s really important to showcase the best of our borough to a national and international audiences. We have such a good story to tell about our borough I am really keen, throughout my mayoral year, to spread the positive messages as wide as possible. It’s in that spirit that, over recent weeks, visitors to the Mayor’s Parlour have included international friends such as the Consulate General of China, the Consulate General of Italy and the Consulate General of Spain. The international flavour was complemented by other lovely visits, including the Assistant High Commissioner of Bangladesh. These distinguished guests really enjoyed their visits, and were particularly impressed by our stunning Grade 1 Rochdale Town Hall. It was an absolute honour and pleasure to meet them. It’s in that international spirit of cooperation, in the true Rochdalian way, that we have such strong relationships with our twin towns and cities. As part of that ongoing and lasting link, I was delighted to welcome the Friends of Tourcoing to the town hall. Rochdale has been formally twinned with the French City since 1956, a long and heartfelt bond of love. We enjoyed afternoon tea and took a trip down memory lane, as well as toasting many more years of friendship. The past pointing the way to an even better future. Many thanks for such a lovely visit. When I became Mayor of Rochdale I gave a commitment to visit all parts of the borough and over the last few weeks I have attended events across all townships. These have included Love Littleborough, Heywood Community Fun Day, MiddFest and a lovely and well attended Rochdale Pride. It was lovely to see so many of you at these important events, showing our borough’s diversity and inclusivity at its very best. As a former veteran, with many years’ service in the Pakistan Navy, I have a strong connection with our local Armed Forces community. I am very proud to have the Armed Forces Breakfast Club as one of mayoral charities. Key forces events I have recently attended include Armed Forces Day flag raisings at Rochdale Town Hall and Middleton Memorial Gardens, Minden Day flag raising and regular visits to the breakfast club. Our local veterans’ community really do represent the very best of us. I was also extremely proud and humbled to award Wing Commander David Forbes with a special mayoral certificate. David has been at the heart of the local armed forces community for many years, serving with great distinction as president of the Rochdale branch of the Royal British Legion. He’s been at the heart of many local initiatives that have grown and expanded over the years, including the breakfast club. There is no one more deserving of mayoral recognition than David. Other key events I have attended over recent weeks have included a charming summer garden celebration at Springhill Hospice; as I said in my last column Springhill is an incredible organisation, caring for patients and loved ones across the borough of Rochdale who are affected by life limiting conditions like cancer, motor neurone disease, and heart failure. We are blessed to have this in incredible organisation in our borough and long may they continue to make every moment count.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: This week's faith news from the Rochdale area St Luke’s Church, Deeplish will hold a service of Morning Praise on August 16 at 10.00 am, officiated by Revd Natty Gray. The service is followed by tea or coffee and a chance to chat. Wednesday, August 19, 11am: Holy Communion service officiated by Revd Pamela Parr. We look forward to welcoming regular members and anyone who would like to join our very friendly, caring congregation. Tomorrow, we’d love you to join us at our altogether service beginning at 10.30am. This week we have a guest preacher. Our friend Richard Stancliffe will be continuing our ‘The Gospel for all’ sermon series in Romans. We’ll be looking at chapter 15 verses 14 to 33. Wherever you’re coming from this week, we’d love to welcome you as we gather together. During the summer we give our children's team a much-needed break and so there will be no Sunday school. Children are very welcome though, there will be activities for our young people to do in church. As well as being a big part of our time together. Whether you’re visiting for the first time or you’ve called St Mary’s home for years, there’s a place for you. On Wednesday evening, we’ll be meeting again to do some jobs around church. No experience necessary, just a willingness to have a go and pitch in. It’s also a great opportunity to get to know one another better. All welcome, please come and join us starting at 6.30pm. If you are interested in what's going on at St M’s, or would appreciate some prayer support head to our website www.stmarysbalderstone.org.uk or please get in touch by e-mail stmarysbalderstone@gmail.com or see our Facebook page, https://www.facebook.com/saintmarysbalderstone/

candidates.source_title: The new Bury NeighbourHub has opened to support residents with work, skills, health, and wellbeing
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
The new NeighbourHub brings help with training and employment, life skills, and wellbeing support closer to local people in Bury.

It gives residents the opportunities to learn new skills, improve their confidence, get online and access help into work, making it easier to improve their prospects and build a brighter future.

The Bury NeighbourHub is a key part of Greater Manchester's Live Well approach, making it easier for residents to access joined-up support, skills, employment and wellbeing services in one convenient community location. By bringing partners together under one roof, it helps people get the right support at the right time, improving opportunities and outcomes for local people.

Bury Council has said that service providers can help with health, wellbeing, or general advice about services from both the Council, as well as other services from other providers, with examples including:

  • Ingeus providing employment and skills support including for young people and ex-offenders and helping people manage physical and mental health conditions
  • Growth Company, a social enterprise that provides employment, training, and business support services
  • The Greater Manchester In-Work Progression Service to help people who are already working but stuck in low-paid, insecure, or part-time jobs move into better roles and increase their earning
  • Bury Adult Learning providing courses leading to qualifications, community classes and employability training
  • NHS partners
  • Citizens Advice Service
  • Social care, support if you are renting privately
  • Bury Care Academy dedicated to supporting, training, and growing the adult social care sector across the borough.
  • Digital inclusion services

Councillor Gavin McGill, Cabinet Member for Culture, Economy and Skills said: “I was really pleased to be at the Neighbourhub launch, it was really busy, really vibrant, and a really impressive venue.

“This is more than just a new location; it's a place where residents can access joined-up support, guidance and opportunities that can make a real difference to their lives. If anyone out there has any need of the services, pop along, you'll get all the help you need for a better life, its a brilliant place.”
candidates.source_summary: The new Bury NeighbourHub has opened in the Millgate shopping centre, having moved from its previous location and expanded its offer.

candidates.source_title: Newport County vs Rochdale Prediction & Betting Tips - Footy Accumulators
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The English Football League welcomes Rochdale back into the fold this weekend after the North West club's lengthy absence following a period of turmoil as they lock horns with Newport County. Newport County finished 20th in League Two last season, surviving relegation by only four points. Many are tipping the Exiles for the drop this season and given the Welsh side's last three league finishes have been 18th, 22nd and 20th, it's not hard to see why. The old proverb argues that teams who consistently flirt with relegation will eventually get their comeuppance, and the feeling is that Newport's is overdue. Results in preseason were underwhelming, with the Welsh side recording three wins, two draws and three losses. Additionally, their opening game in the EFL Cup last weekend saw them lose 5-4 on penalties to Wimbledon following a 1-1 draw. Rochdale, meanwhile, are still riding high following a dramatic promotion from the National League last season. The Dale have been busy in the transfer window, brining in 11 new faces in a hectic summer. They have though, lost manager Jimmy McNulty to Stockport, who has subsequently taken former Dale pair Kyron Gordon (centre-back) and Oliver Whatmuff (last season's on-loan goalkeeper) with him. While these are notable losses, they're not likely to cause Rochdale to struggle this season. The gap between the National League and League Two is arguably the smallest of any gap between any of the country's top five leagues, so the expectation is that Rochdale will survive comfortably this season. Emmanuel Dieseruvwe scored 26 league goals last year and the hope is that he'll be able to provide enough firepower to help secure survival. They've so far retained his services, so he'll likely be key to their chances this season.

candidates.source_title: Cardinal Langley students celebrate 'exceptional' A-Level and BTEC results
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
Cardinal Langley students have received their A-Level and BTEC results, and teachers have praised students, saying that Cardinal Langley students have embraced opportunities beyond the classroom and have made a lasting and hugely positive contribution to school life. They were also commemorated on their academic accomplishments, with that being a testament of everything that they have contributed to the life of the school and the wider local community over their two year course.

This year, students' average UCAS point score has risen again, with 84% of A-Level students achieving grades A*-C grades, and 100% of BTEC grades were awarded at Distinction*, Distinction, or Merit level. This is above the average of 78.4% of grades that were A*-C this year.

Mr Bridson, Headteacher at Cardinal Langley, said: “On behalf of everyone at Cardinal Langley, I would like to offer our heartfelt congratulations to our remarkable Sixth Form students. We are absolutely delighted with this year’s A-level and BTEC results and immensely proud of what our young people have achieved. They have demonstrated outstanding resilience, dedication and ambition. It is particularly pleasing to see so many of them securing places at their first-choice destinations.

“These results represent much more than examination grades. They reflect two years of hard work, determination and personal growth, as well as the encouragement and support provided by our teachers, support staff, parents and carers. Our students have given so much to our school community and we are incredibly proud of the young adults they have become.

“It is a privilege to see them now preparing to take their next steps with such confidence, enthusiasm and optimism. We know they have the ability and character to achieve great things and we wish all of them every success and happiness in the future. I would also like to express my sincere gratitude to our dedicated parents and carers for their continued partnership and to our outstanding staff who work so wholeheartedly to nurture, challenge and support our students every day.”

Some of the students who have received particularly good grades include: Archie, who received grades A*AB, and is going on to study History; Hannah and Lucca, who both achieved an A* in one of their A-Level subjects; and Malachy, Ethan, Alicia, Martina, and Alfie, who all received a Distinction* in one of their BTEC subjects.

 

Chloe achieved two A*s and a Grade B and her twin brother Matthew achieved an A*, a Grade A and a Grade B. They will both be going to Lancaster University to study Biology and Maths respectively.

candidates.source_title: 15-year animal ban for man who kept emaciated dog in squalid Rochdale home - Companion Life
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Paul Lewis Dawson of Brownside Road, Burnley admitted to three animal welfare offences at Tameside Magistrates’ Court on 31 July, including failing to provide a suitable diet, adequate veterinary care and a suitable living environment to a bullbreed called Kano, at an address on Alice Street in Rochdale. The RSPCA began investigating on 6 August last year, following concerns from members of the public that the dog had been left unattended in the property. RSPCA inspector Beth Fazackerley attended the address with Animal Rescue Officer Francesca Iraci, and saw Kano through the keyhole looking very skinny. She knocked and called Dawson but got no response. She pushed wet dog food through the letterbox, which Kano ate. A warrant was obtained with Greater Manchester police, and the officers returned to the address that evening with a police officer and gained entry. Inspector Fazackerley described Kano’s condition: “Kano walked around five metres and then slumped to the ground. He remained on the ground for around 20 seconds and then stood back up. “He was itchy and used his back legs to scratch his chest and rolled around on the grass to get some comfort. His ribs, hip bones, spine and other bones were easily visible and his head appeared angular. I noticed two wounds with scabs on Kano; one above his left shoulder and the other on his right elbow. Both were moist with pus present. “He had sparse fur all over with fur loss concentrated around his hindquarters. His nails were long and his fur and skin appeared dirty with brown crust occurring in multiple places on his body. “The most striking concern was the amount of fleas present on Kano. I have never seen fleas in such large clumps before.”
